I worked out the lexical route's evidence for `w92_leaf` today in two ways that agree. (1) The planted texts: only `app/leaf.py` and `app/middle.py` contain the word. (2) The base clone `7ca16b19df3f` run on a planted store with no code index and the tool not on PATH: it returned `app/leaf.py` 1–2 and `app/middle.py` 1–9, 4–5, 8–9, and the plain fused order is the same. f1's `LEXICAL_PATHS` is now computed in the test from `support.corpus()`, so it stays valid as the code changes, and a comment records the base's answer. I also updated f1's README line. f1's other assertions and every other case are unchanged.

Diff: 2 files, 6 insertions, 4 deletions. Expected set before: {app/leaf.py, app/middle.py, app/top.py}; after: {app/leaf.py, app/middle.py}. `git status --short` is empty. `.git/hooks` holds only `*.sample` files. `python3 -c "import gov; print(gov.__file__)"` gives `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-92-tests/src/gov/__init__.py`.
tests: (1) Run-1 code, the brief's command: **1 failed, 29 passed**. Failing: `test_f3_a_missing_record_store_is_named_and_the_code_routes_evidence_is_returned`, "the whole answer failed for a missing record store: … STORE_MISSING". All three f1 cases pass. (2) The brief's base command (`PYTHONPATH=…/base/src`): 1 failed, 29 passed, identical to (1), because it was still running the worktree's code (see discoveries). (3) A real base run, with the children on the base `src/` through a plugin in my temp folder (`-p at_base`): **17 failed, 13 passed**, which matches the README's red run at the base. Failing: c1, c2, c3, c4, f1 ×3, f2, f3, r1 ×5, r2, r4, u4. At the base each of f1's three cases fails on "the bundle names no state of that route", the facet check, before the evidence assertion is reached. My probe showed the base returns exactly the new expected set for the "never indexed" and "tool not on PATH" form; I did not probe the "tool cannot read it" form at the base separately. (4) `pytest tests --collect-only`: 19084/19086 collected (2 deselected), no collection error.
discoveries: The brief's base command does not test the base. `w2_92_support.Api.env` always sets the children's `PYTHONPATH` to `REPO_ROOT/src`, which is this worktree, by design under DEC-732. Setting `PYTHONPATH` on the pytest command only changes the parent process. To run at the base you have to point `support.SRC` at the base clone; I did that with the plugin `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-92/td2/at_base.py` and wrote nothing in the clone.
risks: none. The expected set comes from the planted text with whole-word matching, which matches the base's tokenisation for this word. If the lexical tokeniser later splits on `_`, `app/top.py` would still not match, because the route needs every word of the question and `top.py` has no `leaf`.
lessons: To measure this suite at the base, override `support.SRC` with a `-p` plugin. Changing `PYTHONPATH` alone measures the worktree again.
proposed_decisions: none
unresolved: My probe's temporary tree `/tmp/gov-os-lead-W2-92/td2/probe-u7q35x0q` is still there. Removing it was refused twice (first `rm -rf` together with `ls`, then `rm -rf` alone, both blocked as needing approval), so I stopped under AR-6. Scratch now: 415 inodes, 5.4 MB, within the budget.
recommended_next_action: The lead can merge `bc7ece7e7db8` into the ticket's worktree; f3 is still the only red at the run-1 code, and the engineer is working on it.
